title: Live AWS account / organization / identity inventory — the Studio has never called STS or Organizations, and its only estate data is a hand-generated snapshot with a hardcoded us-east-1 / aws partition default
why_open: The ledger imports this as FAIL and the code agrees. `grep -rn "GetCallerIdentity|client-organizations|client-sts|client-ecs|client-rds|client-cloudwatch|client-cloudfront|client-acm|client-sqs|client-ses|client-lambda|resourcegroupstagging|cost-explorer"` across apps/ packages/ returns ZERO hits in application code — the only AWS SDK packages declared anywhere are `@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb` + `@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb` (apps/system-studio/package.json:15-16) and `@aws-sdk/client-s3` in apps/web (apps/web/package.json:18-19). `node_modules/@aws-sdk` confirms only dynamodb, s3 and credential-provider packages are installed. So the Studio's runtime identity is never discovered: nothing anywhere calls STS GetCallerIdentity, and no page displays account id, arn, region or partition of the credentials actually in use. What the Studio DOES render is a static snapshot: apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:337-414 renders `estate` out of `apps/system-studio/src/generated/platform-truth.json`, whose `estate.generatedAt` is "2026-07-31T23:40:04.289Z" and whose `account` is the masked literal "1549…97" and `region` the literal "us-east-1". That JSON is compiled by tools/platform-truth.mjs:110-111 from docs/architecture/aws-inventory.json, which is itself produced by tools/aws-inventory.mjs shelling out to the `aws` CLI in a CI workflow — not by the app. And the *estate* that the Studio believes it runs in is guessed, not resolved: apps/system-studio/src/lib/cells.ts:55 `const region = env("AWS_REGION", "us-east-1")` and :65 `partition: env("AWS_PARTITION", "aws")` — the exact `?? "us-east-1"` assumption tests/security/no-hardcoded-estate.test.mjs:1-19 documents as the GE-010-007 data-residency defect, kept green only because cells.ts is on that suite's EXEMPT list (no-hardcoded-estate.test.mjs:33-41). Of the item's own list, tools/aws-inventory.mjs makes NO call at all to: organizations list-organizational-units-for-parent, controltower, sso-admin / identitystore, iam get-role (permission boundaries), organizations list-policies (SCPs), any resource-policy read, cloudtrail, configservice, securityhub, guardduty, inspector2, macie2, detective, budgets, or support — its full call list is lines 67-123 and stops at kms/logs/cloudwatch/backup/cloudformation.
smallest_real_change: Create ONE owning AWS adapter module, `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/client.ts`, that builds every non-DynamoDB client with the DEFAULT provider chain (no credentials option, no region literal — construct `new STSClient({})` and let @aws-sdk/credential-provider-node + AWS_REGION/ECS task role resolve it). Add `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/identity.ts` exporting `resolvedIdentity()` which calls STS GetCallerIdentity ONCE per process (cached, with the same warm-client rationale as registry.ts:50-74), and returns `{ accountId, arn, partition, region }` where partition is parsed from the ARN's second segment (arn:aws:… / arn:aws-us-gov:… / arn:aws-cn:…) and region from the resolved client config (`await client.config.region()`), NEVER from a literal. Render it at the top of /platform as a persistent 'you are looking at account X in region Y, partition Z, as <arn>' header so a developer who swaps the GitHub Action IAM secrets sees the new account with no code change. Then delete the `"us-east-1"` and `"aws"` fallbacks at cells.ts:55,65 — take them from `resolvedIdentity()` and throw `FleetMisconfigured` when neither env nor identity supplies one (cells.ts:41-49 already has that class), and remove cells.ts from the EXEMPT list at no-hardcoded-estate.test.mjs:33-41 so the guard covers it. Add `@aws-sdk/client-sts` and `@aws-sdk/client-organizations` to apps/system-studio/package.json and run `npm install --package-lock-only` — tests/architecture/lockfile-knows-every-workspace.test.mjs is a local catch for this and `npm ci` dies on its first step otherwise. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs:198-207 allows only apps/web/src/lib/s3.ts and apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts to import `@aws-sdk/*`, its AWS_CLIENT_CTORS regex (line 297) already names STSClient/ECSClient/RDSClient/CloudWatchClient/CloudFrontClient/LambdaClient/SQSClient/SESClient, and line 464 asserts `AWS_EXEMPT.size === 0` — so add `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/client.ts` to `OWNERS.aws` with a stated reason and add it to the ownership-proof table at line 396-401, do NOT add it to AWS_EXEMPT. PROOF: a stand-in STS client that (a) returns a us-gov-west-1 arn — assert the page shows partition `aws-us-gov` and region us-gov-west-1, not `aws`/us-east-1; (b) throws AccessDenied on GetCallerIdentity — assert the page renders 'unknown — this role cannot call sts:GetCallerIdentity' and NOT a blank/us-east-1 header; (c) throws a throttle — assert a distinct retrying state. Mutate the PRODUCER: change identity.ts to hardcode `partition: "aws"` and confirm the gov-partition test reds.

title: "Keep day-to-day application workloads out of the Organizations management account" is never checked — nothing in the repo compares the account the Studio runs in against the org's management account
why_open: No code computes or renders this. `grep -rn "MasterAccountId|managementAccount|management account"` across apps/ and packages/ finds only tools/aws-inventory.mjs:133 (`masterAccountMasked`, written into the static docs/architecture/aws-inventory.json by a CI script) — and even that is never compared to anything, never surfaced in the product, and never re-read at runtime. docs/architecture/aws-current-state.md:26-33 states the estate is a single account with Organizations not in use, and apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:361-363 renders exactly one line about it (`estate.organizationInUse ? "in use" : "not in use — a single-account estate"`) from the frozen snapshot — a boolean out of a JSON file, not a check. The Studio therefore cannot answer the one question this item asks: 'is the account I am serving from the same account that owns the organization?' Note this is a READ/verdict item, not an AWS migration: the workload placement itself is external, but the *detection* is a pure read and is entirely absent.
smallest_real_change: In `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/organization.ts`, call Organizations DescribeOrganization and return a discriminated result: `{ state: "IN_USE", managementAccountId, featureSet, rootIds }` | `{ state: "NOT_IN_USE" }` (the API's own AWSOrganizationsNotInUseException — a real answer) | `{ state: "UNKNOWN", principal, action: "organizations:DescribeOrganization", minimumStatement }` on AccessDenied. Add `managementAccountVerdict(identity, org)` in `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/posture.ts` returning `SEPARATED` (identity.accountId !== managementAccountId), `WORKLOAD_IN_MANAGEMENT_ACCOUNT` (equal — the finding), `NO_ORGANIZATION`, or `UNKNOWN`, and render it as a named verdict row on the estate page with the account ids it compared. The verdict MUST be four-valued: collapsing UNKNOWN into SEPARATED would print a reassuring 'workloads are separated' when the truth is the role could not look, which is the STUDIO-000-007 failure this whole surface exists to avoid. PROOF: four stand-in Organizations clients — management account == self (assert WORKLOAD_IN_MANAGEMENT_ACCOUNT and the page names both ids), management account != self (SEPARATED), AWSOrganizationsNotInUseException (NO_ORGANIZATION, and NOT 'separated'), AccessDenied (UNKNOWN plus the iam statement text) — and assert the rendered string DIFFERS in all four. Mutate the producer: make posture.ts return SEPARATED when the org read is UNKNOWN and confirm the fourth test reds.

title: Centralization of trails, Config aggregation, security findings, log immutability, backup policy and CUR is neither read nor verified — no CloudTrail, Config, Backup-policy or CUR call exists anywhere in the repository
why_open: tools/aws-inventory.mjs is the only thing in the tree that talks to AWS outside DynamoDB/S3, and its complete call list (lines 67-123) contains NO `cloudtrail`, NO `configservice`, NO `backup get-backup-vault-access-policy` / `list-backup-plans`, NO `cur describe-report-definitions`, NO `securityhub get-enabled-standards`. It collects `backup list-backup-vaults` only as a list of names (line 122, mapped to bare names at line 219) and the snapshot shows `backupVaults: []`. So the Studio cannot say whether a trail is an organization trail, whether log-file validation is on, whether an S3 log bucket has Object Lock, whether a Config aggregator exists, or whether a CUR is delivered — the six clauses of the requirement. The CUR clause specifically is stranded: apps/system-studio/src/lib/cost-source.ts:43-44 names `FINOPS_CUR_BUCKET`/`FINOPS_CUR_PREFIX`, :46-65 returns NOT_CONFIGURED when they are unset (which they are), and :83-97 has three readers that deliberately `throw`. Nothing anywhere asks AWS whether a CUR/Data Export definition exists — an operator reading 'No Cost and Usage Report is connected' (apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/cost/page.tsx:55-59) cannot tell 'nobody created one' from 'one exists and this role cannot see it'.
smallest_real_change: Add `centralizationPosture()` to `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/posture.ts`: one row per clause — organization trail (cloudtrail DescribeTrails → IsOrganizationTrail, IsMultiRegionTrail, LogFileValidationEnabled), Config aggregation (config DescribeConfigurationAggregators), security findings aggregation (securityhub DescribeHub / GetFindingAggregator), log immutability (s3 GetObjectLockConfiguration on the trail's S3BucketName), backup policy (backup ListBackupPlans + GetBackupVaultAccessPolicy), cost/CUR (cur DescribeReportDefinitions in the payer account). Each row is `{ clause, verdict: "CENTRALIZED" | "LOCAL_ONLY" | "ABSENT" | "UNKNOWN", detail, deniedAction?, minimumStatement? }` — four verdicts, because an AccessDenied on DescribeTrails must render 'unknown — the engine's role lacks cloudtrail:DescribeTrails' and never 'ABSENT'. Wire the CUR row into cost-source.ts so the NOT_CONFIGURED arm can distinguish 'no CUR definition exists' (keep the current operatorSteps at :57-63) from 'a CUR definition exists but FINOPS_CUR_BUCKET is unset' from 'unknown — cannot call cur:DescribeReportDefinitions'; do NOT delete the existing reader shape or the throwing readers at :83-97, they are the correct guard. Register the new clients in `OWNERS.aws` at tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs:198-207 and add the packages via `npm install --package-lock-only`. PROOF, per clause: stand-in returning a single-region non-org trail (LOCAL_ONLY), an org multi-region trail with validation (CENTRALIZED), an empty-but-successful DescribeTrails (ABSENT), and AccessDenied (UNKNOWN + the statement) — assert four DIFFERENT rendered strings. Mutate the producer: make posture.ts treat a denial as ABSENT and confirm the fourth case reds.

title: Alarm semantics do not exist: /platform renders four all-`OK` chips out of a frozen JSON file, and the collector throws away everything that would distinguish INSUFFICIENT_DATA, disabled, stale, missing and unauthorized
why_open: This is the exact defect the requirement names, live in the product. apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:406-413 renders `estate.alarms.map(a => {a.state} {a.name})`. `estate.alarms` comes from apps/system-studio/src/generated/platform-truth.json, which currently holds four entries all with `"state": "OK"` and no other field — and the page even tells the operator at :392-396 that 'the dead-letter alarm below is green because nothing can write to the queue it watches', i.e. it knowingly prints a green alarm that means nothing. Upstream, tools/aws-inventory.mjs:214 is `alarms: list(alarms?.MetricAlarms).map((a) => ({ name: a.AlarmName, state: a.StateValue }))` — it discards `ActionsEnabled` (disabled), `StateUpdatedTimestamp` (stale), and never calls `describe-alarms --alarm-types CompositeAlarm`; and because the aws() helper at tools/aws-inventory.mjs:43-59 returns `null` on failure and `list()` at :61 turns null into `[]`, a denied `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms` produces an EMPTY alarm list that the page renders as 'no alarms' — the precise 'unauthorized rendered as absent' failure. There is no alarm vocabulary anywhere in the app: apps/system-studio/src/components/states.tsx:43-77 declares eleven STATE_KINDS (loading/empty/error/permissionDenied/stale/offline/conflict/archived/partialData/pendingDeletion/highRisk) and none of them is an alarm state; apps/system-studio/src/lib/fleet-health.ts:51-58 defines HealthSignal for tenant LIFECYCLE (serving/resting/stalled/failed/terminal/never-deployed/config-behind) and never touches CloudWatch. Nothing reads CloudWatch at runtime at all.
smallest_real_change: Add `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/alarms.ts` exporting a seven-valued type `AlarmVerdict = "OK" | "ALARM" | "INSUFFICIENT_DATA" | "DISABLED" | "STALE" | "MISSING" | "UNAUTHORIZED"` and `alarmVerdicts({ now, staleAfterMs })` that calls CloudWatch DescribeAlarms (both MetricAlarms and CompositeAlarms) and maps: StateValue OK/ALARM/INSUFFICIENT_DATA straight through; `ActionsEnabled === false` → DISABLED and it OUTRANKS OK (a disabled OK alarm protects nothing); `now - StateUpdatedTimestamp > staleAfterMs` → STALE with the timestamp shown; an expected alarm name absent from a SUCCESSFUL response → MISSING (take the expected set from the alarms Terraform under infrastructure/terraform so 'missing' is falsifiable rather than a hand-typed list); AccessDenied/UnauthorizedOperation on the call → the WHOLE surface is UNAUTHORIZED with principal + `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms` + the minimum IAM statement, and it MUST NOT render an empty list. Give the surface its own named cadence constant (`ALARM_REFRESH_MS`, seconds-scale — cheap and fast-moving, unlike Cost Explorer) and render an explicit 'as of' the way CostReportView.tsx:55 already does. Add a matching status token per verdict in globals.css and a word (not a colour) per verdict, following the states.tsx:16-22 rule; add the new /platform/health route to the ROUTES array at apps/system-studio/e2e/layout.spec.ts:40 and keep the alarm table inside an `overflow-x: auto` container (globals.css:480-487 shows the existing `table.grid` pattern). Fix tools/aws-inventory.mjs:214 to carry actionsEnabled + stateUpdatedTimestamp and to record a denial in `denied` rather than emitting `[]`. PROOF — one stand-in CloudWatch client, five behaviours, five DIFFERENT rendered strings asserted: populated mixed list; empty-but-successful (renders MISSING for each expected alarm, never 'all clear'); ActionsEnabled:false with StateValue OK (renders DISABLED, not OK); StateUpdatedTimestamp 8 days old (STALE with the date); AccessDenied (UNAUTHORIZED naming cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms). Mutate the PRODUCER: change alarms.ts to return `[]` on the AccessDenied branch and confirm the unauthorized test reds; change it to ignore ActionsEnabled and confirm the disabled test reds.

title: No security-findings surface at all — Security Hub, GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config and Access Analyzer are never called, so the Studio's only 'findings' table is a list of documentation gaps compiled from the ledger
why_open: `grep -rn "securityhub|guardduty|inspector2|macie|accessanalyzer|access-analyzer|GetFindings"` over apps/, packages/, tools/ returns nothing except prose. tools/aws-inventory.mjs (the only AWS caller in the repo, calls listed at lines 67-123) makes none of those six calls. The only thing the Studio calls 'findings' is apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:307-335, which renders `truth.findings` — compiled by tools/platform-truth.mjs out of docs/architecture text, i.e. architecture-versus-inventory discrepancies, each with an owning requirement id. Those are documentation findings, not security findings: no severity, no dedupe, no affected tenants, no SLA, no suppression, no remediation state. Every clause of the requirement (dedupe, severity, affected tenants, SLA, ownership, suppression justification/expiry, remediation workflow) has zero implementation. There is also no place to put them: the Studio has no findings store — apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts owns the only DynamoDB access (pk/sk documented at :31-33) and has no finding partition.
smallest_real_change: Add `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/findings.ts` with `securityFindings()` that reads Security Hub GetFindings first (it is the aggregator for GuardDuty/Inspector/Macie/Config/Access Analyzer via ASFF) and falls back to the individual services ONLY where Security Hub reports that product not enabled. Return `{ findings, sources: Array<{ product, state: "AGGREGATED" | "DIRECT" | "NOT_ENABLED" | "UNKNOWN", deniedAction?, minimumStatement? }> }` — the per-source state array is the whole point: with six products, an empty findings list is meaningless unless the page can say which of the six answered, which are off, and which refused. Dedupe on ASFF `Id` + `ProductArn` + `Resources[].Id` (Security Hub re-emits the same finding per update; a naive concat double-counts every GuardDuty finding). Severity from `Severity.Label` (never a numeric guess). Affected tenants by resolving each finding's resource ARN through the Resource Groups Tagging API `tenure:tenant` tag (the same resolver STUDIO-000-008 needs — coordinate, do not duplicate) and mark untagged resources SHARED, never 'unknown tenant → drop'. SLA = severity-band age against `RecordState`/`FirstObservedAt`. Suppression is a WRITE and therefore belongs on the typed-mutation surface with a required typed confirmation and an audit row before the act; keep it out of the read path. Persist suppression justification + expiry as `pk = FINDING#<id>, sk = SUPPRESSION` through registry.ts (add the operation there — forbidden-clients.test.mjs:198-207 forbids a second DynamoDB client, and registry.ts:127-135 already states that rule). Give the surface `SECURITY_REFRESH_MS` as its own named cadence and an explicit 'as of'. Add /platform/security to apps/system-studio/e2e/layout.spec.ts:40. PROOF: stand-in Security Hub client returning (a) a populated multi-product list with two copies of the same finding — assert dedupe leaves one and the count is stated; (b) an empty-but-successful GetFindings with Hub enabled — assert 'no open findings from 6 sources, as of X', not a blank panel; (c) InvalidAccessException (Hub not enabled) — assert NOT_ENABLED and that the page says which products it therefore could not read; (d) AccessDenied — assert UNKNOWN naming `securityhub:GetFindings` and its minimum statement, and assert the findings table is NOT rendered as empty; (e) a throttle — assert backoff and a distinct state. Mutate the producer: drop the dedupe key's ProductArn component and confirm (a) reds.

title: Nothing proves read-only actual state differs from access-denied / missing / stale / error — there is no read-only AWS API in the Studio to prove it about, and the one place denials are shown is a four-entry literal in a generated JSON file
why_open: The requirement is a proof obligation across API and UI, and both halves are absent. API: apps/system-studio/src/app/api contains exactly one route — `auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` (the full tree of apps/system-studio/src/app is app/api/auth, app/platform, app/signin, app/tenants). There is no read-only control-plane API at all, so 'in both API and UI' cannot currently be true of anything. UI: the only denial the Studio renders is apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:73 `const denied = Array.isArray(estate.deniedCalls) ? estate.deniedCalls : []` rendered at :375-390 — three static rows ('organizations describe-organization / Organizations not in use') copied out of a snapshot file, not a live denial, with no principal and no minimum IAM statement. The components to express the distinction exist and are unused for AWS: states.tsx defines PermissionDeniedState (:157-163), EmptyState with its `because` prop distinguishing the two nothings (:118-138), ErrorState (:141-147), StaleState requiring asOf (:166-173) and PartialDataState (:216-227) — but the only consumer of any of them for infrastructure data is the commit-mismatch StaleState at platform/page.tsx:98-106. And the upstream collector actively destroys the distinction: tools/aws-inventory.mjs:43-59 returns `null` on any failure, and `list()` at :61 converts null to `[]`, so 'denied' and 'empty' become the same rendered output. No test anywhere asserts that a denied read renders differently from an empty one.
smallest_real_change: Make the distinction a TYPE that no surface can collapse. In `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/result.ts` define `AwsRead<T> = { state: "ACTUAL"; value: T; asOf: string; fresh: boolean } | { state: "EMPTY"; asOf: string } | { state: "DENIED"; principal: string; action: string; minimumStatement: string } | { state: "STALE"; value: T; asOf: string; ageMs: number } | { state: "ERROR"; code: string; safeDetail: string }` — five arms, no optional `value`, so a caller that forgets DENIED fails `tsc` rather than rendering nothing. Add `readAws(action, fn)` that classifies by the SDK error name (`AccessDenied`/`AccessDeniedException`/`UnauthorizedOperation`/`AuthorizationError` → DENIED; `ThrottlingException`/`TooManyRequestsException` → backoff then ERROR) and NEVER returns EMPTY for a call that threw. Add `AwsReadPanel` to states.tsx rendering one arm each, with DENIED showing principal + action + the minimum IAM statement verbatim so an operator can paste it. Expose the same five arms over HTTP from a read-only `GET /api/aws/[surface]` route (this is also the API half of STUDIO-130-002) with distinct HTTP status + a `state` field in the body — 200 ACTUAL, 200 EMPTY, 403 DENIED, 200 STALE, 502 ERROR — so API and UI cannot drift. PROOF (this item IS the proof, so the test is the deliverable): `apps/system-studio/e2e/aws-unknown-is-not-absent.spec.ts` drives every AWS surface with a stand-in client injected at the client.ts seam, in five behaviours, and asserts for EACH surface that the rendered page text and the API response body are DIFFERENT in all five — specifically that the DENIED rendering contains the action name and does NOT contain the empty-state wording, and that the EMPTY rendering does NOT claim freshness it lacks. Mutate the PRODUCER, not the helper: in each surface module replace its DENIED branch with a return of the EMPTY arm and confirm that surface's case reds; restore and confirm green. Report every mutation and both results — a suite that only exercises `readAws` directly stays green the day a page stops calling it.

title: The Studio has no control-plane API, so opaque ids, pagination, filtering, sorting, field selection, ETags/expected-version, idempotency keys, rate limits, correlation and problem details exist for zero endpoints
why_open: apps/system-studio/src/app/api holds exactly one route — `auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts`. Everything else is a server component reading DynamoDB directly (apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts) or a server action (apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts, .../configuration/actions.ts). None of the ten clauses is implemented for the Studio: there is no pagination helper (apps/web has one at apps/web/src/lib/envelopes/pagination.ts using `MAX_PAGE` from @tenure/contracts, and the Studio does not import it — apps/system-studio/next.config.ts:41 transpiles @tenure/contracts but no Studio source file imports it: `grep -rn "@tenure/contracts" apps/system-studio/src` is empty), no ETag anywhere in the Studio, no idempotency key, no rate limit, no RFC-7807 problem body, and no correlation id (`grep -rn correlationId apps/system-studio/src` → zero hits, while packages/contracts/src/index.ts:126,337,478,813 defines it on four envelope types). registry.ts:136-151 `queryTenantItems` takes a `limit` but returns no cursor, so even the one paginated read cannot be continued. This matters now because the live-AWS read surfaces need an HTTP face that a poller can call without re-rendering a page.
smallest_real_change: Add `@tenure/contracts` to apps/system-studio/package.json dependencies (it is already in next.config.ts:41's transpile list but is NOT a declared dependency — run `npm install --package-lock-only` after, or `npm ci` dies) and build `apps/system-studio/src/lib/api/envelope.ts` on top of its existing `correlationId` field rather than inventing a second envelope. The envelope carries: `items`, an OPAQUE `nextCursor` (base64 of the DynamoDB LastEvaluatedKey or the AWS NextToken — never a raw key, so a client cannot forge a scan position), `asOf`, and `correlationId`. `problem.ts` emits RFC-7807 `{ type, title, status, detail, instance, correlationId }` and is the ONLY way the routes return a non-2xx, so a denial and a throttle are distinguishable by `type` rather than by prose. Serve `ETag` from the digest of the response body and honour `If-None-Match` with 304 — the read surfaces poll, and re-shipping an unchanged ECS service list every few seconds is the throttling the brief warns about. Reject any write route lacking an `Idempotency-Key` header with 400 problem details, and record the key + first response so a retry replays rather than re-acts. Rate-limit per operator + surface with a named per-surface budget (Cost Explorer's must be far lower than ECS's) and return 429 with `Retry-After`. Also extend registry.ts:136-151 to return `{ items, lastEvaluatedKey }` and fix its callers in the same change — the brief's type-widening rule applies: `queryTenantItems` is called from apps/system-studio/src/lib/config-store.ts and apps/system-studio/src/lib/revisions.ts, and both must be updated together. PROOF: e2e asserting a second page differs from the first and the cursor is not decodable to a table key; an If-None-Match replay returns 304 with no body; a duplicate Idempotency-Key returns the first response and the action ran once; an over-budget caller gets 429 + Retry-After; a denied AWS read returns a 403 problem document naming the action, NOT a 200 with `items: []`. Mutate the producer: make the route return the raw LastEvaluatedKey as the cursor and confirm the opacity test reds.

title: Correlation / change / tenant / environment / release / config ids are propagated nowhere in the Studio — the word `correlationId` does not appear once in apps/system-studio/src
why_open: `grep -rn "correlationId|correlation_id" apps/system-studio/src` returns ZERO hits, while packages/contracts/src/index.ts:126, :337, :478 and :813 define `correlationId` as a required field on four envelope types and packages/contracts/src/index.ts:192,393,510,836 validate it — a contract with no Studio consumer. Concretely: apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts issues every DynamoDB command (:141, :161, :191, :265, and the TransactWrite at :275+) with no client request handler and no correlation id, so nothing ties a page render to the AWS calls it made; the Studio's server actions (apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts, .../configuration/actions.ts) mint none; and the lifecycle record that WOULD carry one has no field for it — packages/provisioning/src/execute.ts:56-65 `StepEvidence` is `{ step, state, ok, digest?, detail, checks? }`, with no correlationId, no changeId, no releaseId and no AWS requestId. The only environment/release ids the Studio knows are `BUILD_COMMIT` (apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:77) and `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT` (apps/system-studio/src/lib/cells.ts:56), neither of which is attached to anything it emits. And no AWS resource tag is written by the Studio at all.
smallest_real_change: Add `apps/system-studio/src/lib/correlation.ts` holding an AsyncLocalStorage-backed `currentCorrelation()` seeded once per request from an inbound `X-Correlation-Id` header (validated against the same id rule packages/contracts/src/index.ts:192 uses) or minted with `crypto.randomUUID()`. Attach it in exactly two places so it cannot be forgotten: (1) a `middleware` on every AWS client built in `lib/aws/client.ts`, which stamps the outbound request and CAPTURES the AWS `$metadata.requestId` + `cfId` back into the ambient context — that pairing is what makes an AWS support case answerable; (2) the API envelope and problem document (STUDIO-130-002), so the id a developer sees on screen is the id in the log. Extend `StepEvidence` at packages/provisioning/src/execute.ts:56-65 with required `correlationId` and optional `awsRequestIds: readonly string[]`, and — the brief's type-widening rule — fix EVERY construction site in the same change: packages/provisioning/src/execute.ts:152 (the builder), the persistence in apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts (STEP# rows), the reader at registry.ts getTenant's `evidence` projection, and the fixtures in packages/provisioning's own tests. Emit the id in the AWS resource tag set as `tenure:correlation` when the mutation surface creates anything, alongside `tenure:tenant`. Never put an email, a slug that identifies a school, or any config value into the id or the tag. PROOF: an e2e that reads the correlation id off the rendered page, greps the structured log line for the same id, and asserts the persisted StepEvidence row carries it AND the AWS requestId returned by the stand-in client; a second case sends an inbound X-Correlation-Id and asserts it is honoured rather than replaced; a third asserts a malformed inbound id is rejected, not propagated. Mutate the PRODUCER: make lib/aws/client.ts drop the middleware and confirm the requestId assertion reds — a test that calls `currentCorrelation()` directly would stay green.

title: No change/state-transition record exists for AWS work, and the Studio structurally cannot use `recordAuditEvent` — it is Prisma-bound, which the operator-plane guard forbids the Studio from importing
why_open: The requirement wants every state transition with input/output digest, safe error, AWS request/correlation ids, retries, approvals, evidence and compensation. What exists is packages/provisioning/src/execute.ts:56-65 `StepEvidence = { step, state, ok, digest?, detail, checks? }` — an OUTPUT digest only (no input digest), no safe-error field, no AWS request id, no correlation id, no retry count, no approval reference and no compensation record — persisted as STEP# rows by apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts (partition layout documented at registry.ts:31-33). Worse, the audit path the brief names is unavailable to this app: `recordAuditEvent` lives in apps/web/src/lib/audit-record.ts, which imports `{ Prisma } from "@prisma/client"` at line 4 and `{ db } from "@/lib/db"` at line 16, while tests/security/operator-plane-content.test.mjs:57-69 asserts NO file under apps/system-studio/src imports `@prisma/client` or `@/lib/db`, and :71-85 asserts apps/system-studio/package.json declares neither `prisma` nor `@prisma/client`. So any implementer told to 'write an audit row through recordAuditEvent' will red that guard on their first commit. The reusable half is real and unused here: packages/audit/src/record.ts exports `buildAuditRecord` with hash-chaining (`recordHash`, `sequence`, `previousHash`) and packages/audit/src/verify.ts exports `verifyChain`, and `grep -rn "@tenure/audit" apps/system-studio` finds no importer.
smallest_real_change: Give the Studio its own ledger implementation of the SAME `@tenure/audit` interface, backed by DynamoDB rather than Prisma: `apps/system-studio/src/lib/audit-ledger.ts` exporting `dynamoAuditLedger()` that appends `pk = AUDIT#<partitionDay>, sk = SEQ#<zero-padded sequence>` rows through registry.ts (registry.ts:127-135 states that no second DynamoDB client may be constructed, and forbidden-clients.test.mjs:198-207 enforces it), using `buildAuditRecord` for construction, `redactMetadata` for the metadata blob, and a conditional put on `attribute_not_exists(sk)` so two writers cannot claim the same sequence — that condition is what makes the chain's `previousHash` meaningful. Add `@tenure/audit` to apps/system-studio/package.json (and `npm install --package-lock-only`). Then widen `StepEvidence` at packages/provisioning/src/execute.ts:56-65 to carry `inputDigest`, `safeError?`, `correlationId`, `awsRequestIds?`, `attempt`, `approvalRef?` and `compensation?` — and fix every construction site in the same change (the builder at execute.ts:152, the STEP# writes and the `evidence` projection in apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts getTenant, and packages/provisioning's own test fixtures); the brief's optional-field warning applies exactly here, since a caller that omits `correlationId` compiles silently and produces an unattributable row at runtime. Every mutating AWS operation writes an INTENT row before it acts and an OUTCOME row after, both chained. PROOF: append three records through the real `dynamoAuditLedger` against the local DynamoDB container, tamper with the middle row's `detail` directly in the table, and assert `verifyChain` reports the break at that sequence; assert a concurrent duplicate-sequence write is refused by the condition rather than overwriting; assert an intent row exists even when the AWS call then throws. Mutate the PRODUCER: make the mutation path write the outcome row without the intent row and confirm the 'intent precedes act' test reds.

title: CI retries every Playwright failure once — retry-until-green is configured in both suites — and there is no root command that runs the Studio e2e suite at all
why_open: The requirement is 'deterministic local and CI commands; eliminate flaky retry-until-green behavior'. apps/system-studio/playwright.config.ts:16 is `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0` and apps/web/playwright.config.ts:89 is identical — a test that fails once and passes on the retry is reported as a pass, which is the behaviour the item names. Local and CI are therefore also NOT the same command: a spec that reds locally can green in CI purely by retrying. Second half: the root package.json scripts block defines `studio:dev`, `studio:build` and `studio:type-check` and NO `studio:e2e`, so the suite the brief calls 'the only check that catches a broken Studio route' has no documented entry point — it can only be reached by `npm run e2e --workspace apps/system-studio`, which is not in `npm run verify` (which is `generate && type-check && test --ci && test:platform`) and not in tools/run-platform-tests.mjs. Artifact preservation is the one clause partly met: `trace: "retain-on-failure"` at apps/system-studio/playwright.config.ts:20.
smallest_real_change: Set `retries: 0` in both playwright configs and keep `trace: "retain-on-failure"` (plus add `screenshot: "only-on-failure"`) so removing the retry does not cost the failure evidence. Add a root `"studio:e2e": "npm run e2e --workspace apps/system-studio --"` script — note the trailing `--`, which the scripts block's own leading comment in package.json explains is required or npm eats the forwarded flags — and name it in docs/RUNBOOK.md beside the existing e2e instructions so local and CI run the identical string. Then make the property un-rottable with `tests/architecture/deterministic-test-commands.test.mjs` (node:test, the shape the other 24 specs in tests/architecture use): read every `playwright.config.*` off disk via `git ls-files` and fail if any sets a non-zero `retries`, quoting file:line and the reason (a retried pass is a reported pass). If a spec genuinely reds without the retry, FIX THE SPEC — do not restore the retry; an honest red is the point of the item. PROOF: set `retries: 1` back in apps/system-studio/playwright.config.ts, run `node --test tests/architecture/deterministic-test-commands.test.mjs`, confirm it reds naming that file and line; restore, confirm green. Then run both Playwright suites at retries:0 and report the real pass counts — if anything is genuinely flaky, that is the finding this item exists to surface, and it should be recorded rather than papered over.
